The zoning identification system is based on Method A. The access panels are identified by the zone number in which they are installed and by a suffix of two letters. The suffix is made up of one identification letter and one location letter. The first suffix letter is the primary letter identifying the panel in a logical sequence , i.e., inboard to outboard or front to rear, starting with the letter "A" within each separate zone. The second suffix letter (or locator) identifies the panel in its relation to the aircraft as required, e.g.: - T - Top - B - Bottom - L - Left Hand - R - Right Hand - Z - Internal - F - Floor Panel If all letters of the alphabet are used, panel identification is continued by starting again with the letter "A" and using one of the following as the second letter: - U - Top - D - Bottom - P - Left Hand - S - Right Hand - G - Floor Panel (Chap. 3.4 Para_2.1.1).
The security classification is always "01" (Unclassified). (Chap. 3.6 Para_2.4).
Caveats are not used (Chap. 3.6 Para_2.4).
Only first verification "table-top" is used. The only value allowed for attribute verificationType is "tabtop". (Chap. 3.7 Para_2.1).
Only first verification "table-top" is used. The only value allowed for attribute verificationType is "tabtop". (Chap. 3.7 Para_2.2.2).

For maintenance, repair, support and engineering publications, the language codes are "sx", "es" and "fr". For aircraft operating instructions and MMEL, the languages codes are "en" and "fr". "en" for standard English; "sx" for ASD-STE100 (formerly known as AECMA Simplified English) guidelines; "es" for Spanish; and "fr" for French. (Chap. 3.9.1 Para_2.1).
Warnings, cautions and notes are produced in a individual comrep data module. (Chap. 3.9.3 Para_2).

The AOIs do not use an internal collection of warnings and cautions while the remainder of the infosets use an external collection, using a CIR for warnings and a CIR for cautions. (Chap. 3.9.3 Para_2).

The attribute noteType is not used. (Chap. 3.9.3 Para_2.3).
Title page is not used. (Chap. 3.9.4 Para_2.1).
LOEDM is used for interective publication. LOEP is not used. (Chap. 3.9.4 Para_2.2.1).

Language codes are always used. The following language codes are valid: "en" for standard English; "sx" for ASD-STE100; "es" for Spanish; and "fr" for French. Country codes are always used. Country code is "CA" or "ZZ" when Language code is "fr" and "ZZ" when Language code is "en", "sx" or "es". (Chap. 3.9.5.1 Para_2.1.1.3).
Draft data modules are not allowed to exchange. (Chap. 3.9.5.1 Para_2.1.1.4).
The issue date is the date of the revision (linked to the revision cycle agreed by the Customer). The year must lie between "2000" and "2099" inclusive. (Chap. 3.9.5.1 Para_2.1.2.1).
